Seminar Title:

Detection and Prevention of Malware and Vulnerabilities in Software Systems

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Computer Science and Engineering

Speaker Name:

Manoj Kumar Mahanta

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall (CS-114)

Date and Time:

07 Sep 2026 04:15 PM

Contact:

Panthadeep Bhattacharya, PIC Seminar

Abstract:

Software systems face two closely coupled security threats: malicious software attacking from outside, and vulnerabilities that remain latent within the software itself. Both are moving targets. Signature-based detectors and rule-driven static analyzers are increasingly inadequate, as adversaries use obfuscation, packing and adversarial perturbation to evade them, while newly disclosed vulnerabilities grow each year. An initial study in this direction produced a multi-architecture deep learning detector for Windows PE malware, hardened by multi-attack adversarial training, which showed that the accuracy-robustness trade-off depends on the architecture chosen rather than holding universally. The proposed research builds on this to investigate learning-based methods for securing software artefacts more broadly, drawing on techniques such as deep architectures, graph-based code models, large language models and explainable AI. The research directions include robustness under adversarial and evolving threat conditions, generalization across file formats, platforms and code representations, interpretability of model decisions for security analysts, and the progression from detection towards prevention. The expected outcome is a unified and practically deployable framework for securing modern software systems.
